potential-energy.def: Energy stored in the configuration of a system of objects that interact through conservative forces; it belongs to the system, not to one object.

conservative-force.def: A force whose work depends only on the start and end positions (gravity, an ideal spring). A force whose work depends on the path, like kinetic friction, is nonconservative.

gravitational-pe.def: The potential energy of an object-Earth system near Earth's surface: ΔU_g = mgΔy.

elastic-pe.def: The potential energy stored in a stretched or compressed ideal spring: U_s = ½k(Δx)², with Δx measured from the relaxed length.

zero-point.def: The configuration chosen to have zero potential energy; any choice works because only changes in potential energy matter.

universal-gpe.def: The gravitational potential energy of two masses at any separation: U_G = −Gm₁m₂/r, zero at infinite separation.
